name: Thumb-first thread: a 240vh hero, a thread that peels off the mark, and a merge that always completes
summary: Design premise: a phone visitor reads the first screen for 3-6 seconds, then flicks. Each flick is 70-90vh. So the whole cloche story must land in two flicks and the thread must be running beside the page by the third: the pin is 240lvh (frame stuck for 140vh of scroll), not 350. At rest nothing moves: the words sit on near-black ground with the blurred cloche glowing beneath them; the first flick pulls focus (a pre-blurred still crossfades out over the sharp film: no runtime filter of any kind), the second lifts the lid while the camera pulls back so the whole mark is on screen under the header; the thread wakes at the mark's LEFT lobe, peels off in one S to the rail at x=10 (the gutter's middle), waits a beat, and the moment the frame un-sticks the page line continues it with its head pinned at 60% of the screen, so the line grows exactly as the reader scrolls and never runs ahead of the eye. The rail wanders +/-4px (crest at every headline, trough at every prop) and crosses the full-bleed stills and the before/after plates on a black case stroke. At the branding section the head enters the real mark's left lobe, draws the figure-eight in the rail's colours over 12vh of scroll, and the merge itself (ring thickens to the ribbon, takes the mark's own sweep, real mark fades in, the wordmark rule draws) is a one-shot 1.1s timed sequence fired when the loop closes and reversed if the reader backs off, so no reader is left with a half-merged lockup. Three tiers: A = WebCodecs film (0.75 MB phone encode, frames 0-183, 720x900), B = two stills (blurred frame 0 dissolving into sharp frame 183) with the identical thread and merge, C = today's static story (reduced motion, fine pointer, desktop). Everything is under html.story.pfilm; no html.film rule changes; copy untouched.

heroLayout:
DOM (index.tpl.html only, then build_index.py; index.html is never edited). The head gate script gets `window.__PHONE = '(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 1024px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)'` and adds `pfilm` to beside `story` when it matches (and no Save-Data/2g), so the pinned layout exists before first paint: no flash of the stacked story, correct scroll restoration on reload, LCP measured on the right layout. Inside #heroFrame, after the canvas, add `` (the site's own desktop-skip pattern; a desktop fetches 1 gif byte). Default `.hero__blur{display:none}`. At arm time site.js wraps #heroVideo, #heroFilm and .hero__blur in one JS-made `
` (reparenting keeps the WebGL context) and appends ` (hero-mark-m.jpg, sharp frame 183, 720x900 q6 ~45 KB, fetched after load with priority low) whose opacity = smooth(u,.58,1.0); the lift becomes a dissolve from blurred cloche to sharp mark. Tier A also loads hero-mark-m.jpg lazily as a safety net: while !heroReady its opacity follows the same curve, so a reader who flicks past u=1 before the 0.75 MB film arrives sees the mark, never a black box; when the film lands the canvas paints frame 183 first (identical picture) and the still fades over .3s.
filmPlacement:
ASSET. Phone encode from cloche3d/out PNGs: `crop=864:1080:864:0,scale=720:900:flags=lanczos` (centre x 1296 = 67.5%, matching the stills' object-position; mark box in crop coords x .11-.88, y .35-.72, centre (.50,.53); closed cloche x .18-.98), frames 0-183 only (`-frames:v 184`, 0-6.1s, 23 GOPs of 8: the lid lift is over by 4.2s and the mark is alone and still from 5.8s, so 6.1s is the resting pose with a margin; nothing of 6.1-9.6s, including the bottom-right opening at 7.8s and the up-right unravel, is in the file: constraint 4 by construction). Same recipe as encode.sh (x264 High 4.0, keyint 8, keyint_min 8, sc_threshold 0, bf 0, bt709 tv, timescale 15360, faststart) at crf 25, preset veryslow: ~0.75 MB (measured 990 KB for 247 frames at crf 25; 184 frames is ~25% less). Stills: hero-still-m.jpg = frame 0 at the same crop, 432x540, gblur sigma 7, q 5 (~20 KB, the LCP-capable poster); hero-mark-m.jpg = frame 183 sharp, 720x900, q 6 (~45 KB). Register the three files in stamp.js's token lists.

BOX MATH (layoutFilm(), once per orientation and after fonts). Encode (fw,fh) = (720,900); mark fraction (mx,my) = (.50,.53), markW = .77. Screen (bw,bh) = (frame.clientWidth, frame.clientHeight = LVH). MARKW = .72, MARKY = .40. s = min(MARKW*bw/(markW*fw), .85*bh/fh); dw = fw*s; dh = fh*s; bl = bw/2 - dw*mx; bt = MARKY*bh - dh*my. 390x844: s = .5068, box 365x456 at (12.5, 96), mark 281 px wide with centre (195, 338). 360x780: s = .4678, box 337x421, mark 259. 430x932: s = .559, box 402x503, mark 310. 768x1024 (portrait tablet, coarse): s = .997, box 718x897, mark 553 (the 720 store shown ~2x at dpr 2: soft but it is a glowing mark; acceptable, an 864x1080 encode chosen by a third media query is the upgrade if Karan minds). Landscape phone 844x390: s = min(.72*844/554, .85*390/900 = .368) = .368, box 265x331, mark 204 px: small but whole; the text row uses svh so the buttons stay above the fold.

TRANSFORM BY SCROLL (compositor only; the box's layout never changes on the scroll path): --hz = 1.25 - .25*smooth(u,.58,1.00); --hy = (.16*LVH)*(1 - smooth(u,.58,1.00)) px, transform-origin 50% 53% = the mark's centre, so at u=0 the mark-centre origin sits at .40*LVH + .16*LVH = 56% of the screen and the box (456x570) spans y 171-741 (the blurred dome at ~376-627, behind the buttons and below), and by u=1.0 the whole mark is inside the width at 40% with the lid's exit clear of the header. One CSS rule drives the canvas, the blur still, the mark still and the feather together because they are children of the box.

FILM CLOCK. t(u) = track(PT, u), PT = [[0,0],[.22,.6],[.58,1.8],[1.00,4.2],[1.12,6.1],[1.40,6.1]], u = clamp(scrollY / LVH, 0, 2.5) (clamped first: iOS rubber-band gives negative scrollY and a burst on snap-back; while y < 0 direction changes are ignored so filmDir does not flip). The lift (.58 -> 1.00 u, 354 px of scroll for 72 frames = 4.9 px/frame) is denser than the desktop's 10 px/frame on purpose: one flick shows the lid rise in ~0.6 s after the lerp. Per rAF: phoneT = t(pShown); if (FD) filmFrame(phoneT) [wantFrame, paintFrame, pumpDecoder exactly as desktop] else tier B opacity. Canvas store stays at the encode's 720x900 (sizeFilmCanvas phone branch: viewport 720x900, ts 1/720,1/900, bc 0 = bilinear; the compositor scales; no dpr resize ever, so the store is never cleared by a toolbar collapse). keepGops = 3 on the phone (24 frames, ~23 MB) so a hardware decoder's buffer pool is never starved. Decoder config on the phone: isConfigSupported for hardwareAcceleration 'prefer-software' then 'no-preference', first supported wins (desktop keeps prefer-software untouched). Slow-decoder bail-out on the phone at 250 ms/GOP -> tier B, never the <video> element.

READINESS. heroReady only after the first paintFrame; until then --hb is held at 1 (the blurred still stays) and the mark still covers u > .58; once ready, paint frame t(u) first, then release --hb toward its curve over .3 s. Poster/first paint order: still (parse-time <picture>), then site.js arms and fetches the MP4 after the load event with fetch(url,{priority:'low'}), whole-file read (0.75 MB, 20 s watchdog; abort -> tier B, not video-failed).
blurMethod: Opacity crossfade of a pre-blurred still over the sharp film, nothing else. hero-still-m.jpg is frame 0 at the encode's exact crop, gaussian sigma 7 at 432x540 (upscaled 1.05-1.4x on screen, so it reads as a ~16-20 px blur at 390 wide), inside the same transformed box as the canvas, layered ABOVE the canvas at opacity --hb. --hb = heroReady ? 1 - smooth(u,.10,.45) : 1. Because the film holds frame 0 until u=.22 and the still IS frame 0, the crossfade reads as a focus pull on one picture; the faint steam that starts at u=.22 fades in under a still that is already 60% gone. Cost: one static image layer, rasterised once, no per-frame work; it doubles as the poster before the MP4 arrives and as tier B's first still. Legibility comes from the frame scrim (rgba(10,10,10) .90 to 60vh, .55 at 72vh, .30 at 100vh, opacity --hs = 1 - .70*smooth(u,.12,.55)) and from the layout itself: at u=0 the box begins at y 171 with a feathered top, so the h1 sits on plain #0A0A0A ground; only the sub and the buttons are over the blurred bokeh, worst backdrop #171411 under the .90 scrim (ink 15:1, ink-2 5.5:1, ink-3 4.8:1, acc 5.9:1; button ink on acc 6.4:1 unaffected). NOT: CSS filter:blur() on the canvas (2-6 ms per changed frame on a 1.3 Mpx layer at dpr 2, and iOS re-rasterises the layer), not backdrop-filter anywhere near the frame (the header's own backdrop-filter is switched off under pfilm while the frame is stuck), not an SVG filter, not a mip-level shader blur (needs painter changes the desktop shares; the still does the job for free), not a baked-blur encode (the revealed mark must be crisp and the blur must go away). Optional toggle for Karan's comparison habit: ?pfilm=cssblur applies filter:blur(var(--hb-px)) to the box instead, capped at 10 px, class removed at u > .45; kept behind the toggle only.
lineBirth:
WHERE. Not the mark's centre (a line from the middle of a closed ring reads as 'from nowhere'): the thread peels off the ring's LEFT lobe at its outer extreme, where the ribbon is vertical, so a downward tangent is the ribbon's own direction. Frame-local (390x844, settle geometry): mark rect x 54-336, y 256-424; E_mark = (markLeft + .09*markW, markCentreY) = (79.3, 338). Rail x xr = gut/2 = 10 (read from getComputedStyle(stage).paddingLeft; 11 on a 22 px gutter). Reading line K = .60: R0f = (xr, .60*LVH) = (10, 506).

WHEN. Wake: glow = smooth(u,1.12,1.20); the tip (72 px radial disc: #FFF8EC core 2.2 px, rgba(255,240,214,.6) at 3.6 px, .24 at 9 px, .07 at 20 px, 0 at 36 px) sits on E_mark at opacity .6*glow with a breath scale 1 + .12*sin(now*.0039) (1.6 s period). Birth: b = smooth(u,1.20,1.34); birth = 1 - (1-b)^2 (ease-out: it leaves fast, settles gently). Rest: 1.34 -> 1.40 the tip breathes at R0f. Un-stick at u = 1.40 (PIN = 2.4). The 6vh rest is deliberate: a beat of stillness at the edge before the page takes the thread.

THE CURL (#snkCurl inside <svg class="snkc"> appended to .hero__frame, width/height/viewBox = frame px, so it stays with the pinned mark and then scrolls away with the frame). With dx = E.x - xr, dy = R0f.y - E.y (69.3, 168): c1 = (E.x, E.y + .40dy); c2 = (xr + .55dx, E.y + .38dy); A = (xr + .30dx, E.y + .58dy); c3 = A + .6*(A - c2); c4 = (xr, E.y + .82dy); d = M E C c1 c2 A C c3 c4 R0f. On 390x844: M79.3 338 C79.3 405 48.1 401.8 30.8 435.4 C20.4 455.6 10 475.8 10 506; Lc = getTotalLength() ~ 200 px. It drops from the lobe, drifts left in one lazy S ('like a snake'), and arrives at the rail with c4 directly above R0f so the tangent is exactly vertical: the page line continues it with round caps overlapping, no seam. Drawing: the four-thread stack (case 5 px #000 .55, glow 10 px url(#snkglitc) .16, body 2.2 px url(#snkgc), core .8 px #FFF6E8 .5) as <use>s of #snkCurl in a <g> with stroke-dasharray:var(--L); stroke-dashoffset:var(--off); shownCurl lerps toward birth (k = 1 - .8^(dt/16.667), snap < .003), --off = Lc*(1 - shownCurl) quantised .5 px. Colour: the curl's gradients are vertical userSpaceOnUse copies of the page gradient phase-shifted into frame space (y1c = y1 + fy0 - frameRestTop), so at E_mark the stroke is spectrum stop .55 (cyan), the colour of the film mark's left lobe in frames 5.8-8.0 s: the thread is visibly the same light as the ring it leaves. The tip rides atL(curlMap, shownCurl*Lc) with page position = curl point + (scrollY - fy0) while stuck. Why the film's own bottom-right opening (frames 233-239) is NOT used: it opens at the lower RIGHT of the ring while our thread leaves at the LEFT; showing both would read as two different things happening to one mark. The ring stays whole: an infinity mark sends a strand out and, at the end of the page, the strand finds the mark again. That is the story the reader gets without reading a word.
linePath:
SPACE. Page px relative to section.film's top-left (fy0 = film top + scrollY, ~0); <svg class="snk" id="snk"> appended to section.film after .stage, width=W height=H viewBox="0 0 W H" as attributes (W = film.clientWidth, H = film.offsetHeight; never % and never transformed; absolutely positioned so it never feeds the ResizeObserver that rebuilds it), z-index 3, pointer-events:none, overflow:visible, no will-change (a 390x7000 px promoted layer at dpr 3 would be a 24 Mpx texture; unpromoted, Chrome re-rasterises only the tiles whose dash offset changed).

ANCHORS. LVH = heroFrame.offsetHeight (100lvh, stable under the URL bar). heroTop = pageTop(.hero) (~0). frameRestTop = heroTop + (PIN - 1)*LVH = 140vh. R0 = (xr, frameRestTop + K*LVH - fy0) = (10, page 200vh): the curl's end in page space at the instant the frame un-sticks. Amplitude A = min(4, gut*.2) = 4 px: the gutter is 20 px, text begins at x=20, the body must never cross x=16; the glow (x 5-15) may kiss the card borders at .16 opacity, which is fine.

KEYPOINTS (measured by buildSnake(), rebuilt by a debounced ResizeObserver on .film + .act--mark, document.fonts.ready, the storymark's load, and the 140 ms resize): a crest (xr + A) at the top of every .band__in of a non-hero band (getBoundingClientRect + scrollY; bands are never transformed) and a trough (xr - A) at the layout top of every .act except .act--still/.act--mark/.act--word (offsetTop chain, because .act carries translateY(18px) until .in). Keep those with y in (R0.y + 60, S0.y - .25*LVH), sorted; when consecutive points are more than .6*LVH apart insert floor(gap/.6LVH) intermediates alternating sides (the four cards and the two 4:5 stills get their own wander); drop any point within 24 px of the previous. Append (xr, S0.y - .25*LVH) and S0 = (xr, E.y - 1.15h) so the last half wave damps onto the rail before the entry. Cubics by Catmull-Rom (c1 = Pi + (Pi+1 - Pi-1)/6, c2 = Pi+1 - (Pi+2 - Pi)/6, ghost ends repeated). Because every keypoint's y strictly increases and x stays within xr +/- 4, the rail is monotone in y, which the drawing law needs. Full-bleed props (the two sky figures at margin-inline calc(var(--gut)*-1), the pair) are crossed at x=10 on purpose: the case stroke lifts the thread off the clouds and the dining rooms.

ENTRY. The real mark: force `html.story.pfilm .act--mark{transform:none}` before measuring (else the loop lands 18 px low); R = .storymark rect (390: w = min(62vw,280) = 242, h = 242*397/720 = 133, Rl = 74). From mark-720.webp's geometry (ribbon .178w thick; centreline extremes at .090w/.910w, lobe tops/bottoms at .161h/.839h): P(sx,sy) = (Rl + .090w + (sx - 8)*.00445w, Rt + .161h + (sy - 16)*.00770h) maps the #loop symbol (x 8..192, y 16..104). E = P(8,60) = (95.8, cy), where the loop's tangent is straight down. The rail's last segment: C (xr, E.y - .5h) (E.x, E.y - .6h) E: vertical out of the gutter, vertical into the lobe's left edge. Ls = #snkPath.getTotalLength() (~6-7 k px on 390).

THE LOOP. #snkLoop = #loop re-based to start at the left extreme heading down: M P(8,60) C P(8,84) P(26,104) P(52,104) C P(78,104) P(100,88) P(100,60) C P(100,32) P(122,16) P(148,16) C P(174,16) P(192,36) P(192,60) C P(192,84) P(174,104) P(148,104) C P(122,104) P(100,88) P(100,60) C P(100,32) P(78,16) P(52,16) C P(26,16) P(8,36) P(8,60) Z: the left lobe's lower half, the crossing, the right lobe clockwise, back through the crossing, the left lobe's upper half. Every control point mapped by P() so the d is in page px (no transform attribute: dash lengths and --lw must be px). Ll = getTotalLength() (~470 px on 390).

COLOUR. Two vertical userSpaceOnUse gradients (x1=x2=0, spreadMethod repeat) with the desktop's eight #specg / #specglit stops. Phase anchors: at the birth (markPageY = frameRestTop + 338 - fy0) the stroke shows stop .55 (cyan, the film's left lobe); at E.y it must show stop .26 (yellow: what #infg paints at the real mark's left extreme, diagonal parameter ~.25), so the join is colour-continuous. span = E.y - markPageY; cycles = max(1, round(span/(1.5*LVH) - .71)); Pp = span/(cycles + .71); y1 = markPageY - .55*Pp; y2 = y1 + Pp. ~one full rainbow per 1.5 screens down the page.
lineDrawingLaw:
READING LINE. The drawn end (the head) is pinned at K = .60 of the screen: tipY = scrollY + .60*LVH - fy0 (page px). Why .60: the eye reads the upper-middle, the thumb rests on the lower third, the contact bar sits at 92%+; at .60 the head is above the thumb and just above the next headline as it climbs into view, so the line always looks like it is leading the reader down, never trailing.

TARGET. target = tipY <= R0.y ? 0 : atY(lineMap, min(tipY, E.y)), where lineMap = sample(#snkPath, max(300, round(Ls/8))) (the desktop's sample(): xs, ys, ls, L at ~8 px spacing; built once per rebuild, never getPointAtLength per frame) and atY is a binary search on the y-monotone ys returning the interpolated arc length. Because target is a single-valued function of scrollY, a flick draws forward through every point and a scroll back rewinds through the same points: the thread is a scrub, like the desktop bolt.

LERP. shownL += (target - shownL)*(1 - .8^(dt/16.667)) with dt = min(100, now - last), snapped when |target - shownL| < .25 px; the same for shownCurl (toward birth) and shownLoop (toward lt, k base .85 so the loop draws a hair slower, plus a floor: the loop may not advance faster than Ll/500 ms so a flick past the mark still shows the circuit being drawn). dt-normalised so 30 / 60 / 120 Hz feel the same. One rAF loop kicked by a passive scroll listener; it runs while any of the three is unsettled or while the tip breathes (u in [1.12,1.40] and hero on screen), then stops. The IntersectionObserver on .hero (rootMargin 10%) cancels the breath off screen.

WRITES. stroke-dasharray:var(--L) stroke-dashoffset:var(--off) on each <g> (inherited by the four <use> threads); --off = L - shown via setVar quantised to .5 px, so a settled frame writes nothing. --off is the only per-frame style change on the page-tall svg. The tip: transform translate3d(x,y,0) scale(s) + opacity from atL(map, shown) (binary search on ls; page px; on the curl: frame px + (scrollY - fy0)). Tip states: hidden (u < 1.12) -> on E_mark breathing -> on the curl -> on R0f breathing -> on the rail head -> on the loop head -> fades with the merge (opacity .9*(1 - lb)).

LOOP FRACTION. lt = clamp((tipY - E.y)/(.12*LVH), 0, 1): 12vh of scroll draws the circuit (101 px on 844): short on purpose, so a reader who stops with the mark anywhere in the middle of the screen has a closed ring. --off = Ll*(1 - shownLoop).

REBUILD RULE. On any geometry rebuild, shownL and shownLoop are re-derived from the new maps at the same tipY (no lerp across a geometry change); shownCurl is carried over. Programmatic jumps (header anchor links with html scroll-behavior:smooth): set a jumping flag from click until scrollend (Chrome 114+) or 120 ms quiet; while jumping the film paints only the nearest already-decoded frame and does not pump ahead; the line still lerps (it is cheap).

HERO VARS. Same rAF: --hb, --hs on .hero / frame; --hz, --hy on .hero__box; all via setVar with steps .01 / .01 / .002 / .5px so settled frames write nothing. No getBoundingClientRect on the scroll path: heroTop, LVH, frameRestTop, R0, E, h, maps are cached by buildSnake().

RESOLVE LAYOUT (html[data-v="editorial"].story.pfilm only; the reduced-motion story keeps today's resolve): .band--resolve .band__in{text-align:center} .band--resolve{padding-bottom:28px} .act--mark{padding:8px 0 0;transform:none} .storymark{width:min(62vw,280px);opacity:var(--rb,0);transition:none} (img.loading set to 'eager' when pfilm arms so the merge target is decoded before the thread arrives) .act--word{padding:14px 0 48px} .act--word .rule{transform:scaleX(0)} .act--word.is-drawn .rule{transform:scaleX(1);transition:transform .9s var(--ease-out)} (transform-origin left already set). Headline 3 x 42 px + 28 + 8 + mark 133 + 14 + wordmark 31 + 16 + rule 2 = 351 px: the whole lockup fits one 844 screen above the bar, so the merge is always seen whole. .act--mark's story reveal (.in translateY) is overridden to none under pfilm; the story's own opacity reveal is replaced by --rb.

ARRIVAL. The head reaches E = (Rl + .09w, cy) when scrollY = cy - .60*LVH (~795vh on 390x844); the mark is then at 60% of the screen, wordmark at ~68%, bar at 92%: no overlap. The loop <g> holds three threads of #snkLoop: lglow (url(#infg), width --lw*2.6, opacity .14*(1 - --lb)), lbody (url(#snkg): the rail's colours arrive, opacity 1 - --la), lring (url(#infg): the mark's own sweep, opacity --la*(1 - --lb)); --lw starts at 2.4 px. It draws clockwise from the left lobe over 12vh of scroll (lerped, floor 0.5 s/circuit). At the entry the rail shows stop .26 (yellow) = what #infg shows at the left extreme, so nothing changes colour at the join.

THE MERGE IS TRIGGERED, NOT SCRUBBED. When shownLoop >= .995 a merge clock m runs 0 -> 1 over 1100 ms (ease-in-out, rAF-driven); if shownLoop falls below .6 it runs 1 -> 0 over 500 ms. From m: la = smooth(m,0,.55) (the ring takes the mark's sweep and thickens: --lw = 2.4 + (.178w - 2.4)*la, i.e. 2.4 -> 43 px at w 242, the ribbon's real thickness in mark-720.webp), lb = smooth(m,.40,1) (the drawn ring fades out while the real mark fades in: --rb = lb on .act--mark), at m >= .70 .act--word gets is-drawn (the rule draws from the left over .9 s, the desktop's own gesture), the tip dies with .9*(1 - lb), and the rail group's opacity eases to .35 over the same 1.1 s (once; not per frame) so the mark is the only bright thing. Why triggered: on the phone the text acts already reveal by time when they enter the viewport (.in), so a timed merge IS 'the same as the text does' here; and a pure scroll scrub would leave a reader who stops with the mark at 45% of the screen looking at a half-thick, half-faded ring until they scroll on. With the trigger every reader who reaches the mark sees the whole merge in ~1.4 s and can scroll back to unmake it. State exposed: window.__pfilm.merge() = m.

AFTER. The thread ends at the mark: no line in SEE IT IN ACTION, the work section, the picker, the form or the footer (#snk's path stops at E; nothing is drawn below the resolve). The wordmark DOMIN8TE MEDIA and the rule stay as today's markup and copy.

performance: Per scroll frame (tier A, 390x844 mid-range Android, target <= 6 ms JS + GPU under 12 ms on the 4x-throttled CDP run): 1 texture upload of 720x900 (0.65 Mpx) + 1 quad at the native store, bilinear (bc 0), compositor scale; <= 4 custom-property writes on the hero (--hb --hs --hz --hy, each quantised, zero when settled); <= 3 dash-offset writes (curl, rail, loop) quantised .5 px; 1 tip transform + opacity; 2 binary searches. No layout reads on the scroll path (everything cached by buildSnake/layoutFilm). No filter, no backdrop-filter (the header's is off while the frame is stuck), no mask-image, no mix-blend-mode, no will-change on the page-tall svg, no per-frame transform on any svg; the only promoted layers are the box (transform), the tip and the fixed chrome. Decode: 8-frame GOPs, keepGops 3 = 24 open frames (~23 MB I420 at 720x900 vs ~100 MB with the desktop file), dropped on visibilitychange and when hero.off (scrollY > 240vh + 40 px), refilled by pDraw on return. Bytes: 0.75 MB MP4 held as one Uint8Array (whole-file read: every seek local; no Range dance with the Hostinger CDN); still 20 KB (parse-time, fetchpriority high, LCP candidate with the h1); mark still 45 KB after load. Network: MP4 fetched after the load event with priority low, so fonts and the still win the first seconds; on 4G ready in ~1-2 s, inside the 3-6 s a reader spends on the first screen; if not ready by the time they scroll, the still and the mark still cover every u. Idle: rAF stops when the three lerps settle and the tip is not breathing; the breath (u 1.12-1.40) runs only with the hero on screen (IntersectionObserver). Listeners: scroll {passive:true} records nothing but scheduling; no touch listeners; touch-action default. Sticky frame: 100lvh constant, so the URL-bar collapse never resizes the canvas store; the resize handler ignores height-only changes < 25%; orientation change (matchMedia portrait change + 140 ms resize) re-runs layoutFilm + buildSnake, store untouched. Rasterisation: #snk (390 x ~7400 px) is unpromoted; only tiles whose dash offset changed re-raster (~2-3 tiles per frame near the head). Page-scroll cost elsewhere is today's story: IntersectionObserver reveals only. Probe: gauntlet/pfilm-check.js with cdp.js at 390x844 touch dpr 3 (and 360x780, 430x932, 844x390, 768x1024): wait .hero.video-ready <= 8 s, scroll to u = 0,.22,.58,1.0,1.12,1.20,1.34,1.40 asserting __pfilm.frame() within 2 of 0,18,54,126,183,183,183,183, --hb 1 -> 0, --hz 1.25 -> 1, sticky frame rect.top === 0 through the pin, tip page y = scrollY + .60*LVH between s0 and E, getComputedStyle(heroFrame).position === 'sticky', scrollWidth === innerWidth, no console errors; then a scripted 8000 px scroll in 60 steps with rAF deltas (frame time < 12 ms at 4x CPU throttle; if the sharpen phase exceeds it there is nothing to trim on the phone because the blur is a static image, so look at the decoder); reduced-motion run asserts no pfilm and the .act--still visible; desktop 1440x900 no-touch run asserts no pfilm, __pfilm.on() === false, heroSrc === desktop URL and an empty ImageChops bbox against pre-change stills. One real iPhone (Safari 16.4+: WebCodecs + WebGL VideoFrame upload, sticky, lvh) and one mid Android (Chrome + Samsung Internet: decoder config chosen, toolbar behaviour) read __pfilm.state() from the inspector or the hidden ?pfilm=dbg readout.
risks: position:sticky inside the absolute .hero under the flex .stage: html/body overflow-x:clip on the root is fine, but any overflow on main/.film/.stage kills the pin silently. Verify on the first 390x844 run (frame rect.top must read 0 through the pin) and on the iPhone; fallback: the driver already knows u, so it can switch the frame to position:fixed while 0 < u < 1.4 and back to absolute at the ends.

iOS Safari 16.4-16.x: VideoDecoder exists but texImage2D(VideoFrame) may throw; today's blit catch would abandon the decoder. Phone-gated retry through a cloned 2D canvas + drawImage(VideoFrame), then tier B (stills), never the <video> element. Cannot be driven from this Windows machine: one real-iPhone check of __pfilm.state().twoD is required.

Safari decodes through VideoToolbox regardless of the hint; a hardware flush per 8-frame GOP is 20-60 ms, occasionally more. The phone threshold is 250 ms/GOP and the bail-out is tier B, so a slow device loses the lid motion, not the thread; revisit only with numbers from a device.

Hardware decoder buffer pools: 24 open VideoFrames (keepGops 3) is inside MediaCodec's usual 8-16 output buffers only if the decoder copies out; if a device stalls (flush never resolves) drop to keepGops 2 and, as the next step, upload-and-close (cache GL textures instead of frames), which touches the shared decoder and is deliberately not in v1.

The 0.75 MB film arriving after the reader has scrolled: covered by the still (--hb held at 1 until ready) and the lazily loaded mark still for u > .58, then a first paint at t(u) and a .3 s fade; if the reader is already past 240vh the decoder is not started at all for this visit (hero.off), which saves the memory.

Sticky pin + Android Chrome scroll anchoring on reload mid-page: the pinned band's height exists from the head gate (html.pfilm before first paint) so anchoring has nothing to correct; if a device still jumps, set overflow-anchor:none on .band--hero only.

Desktop parity: the changes touch shared functions (sizeFilmCanvas, blit, initHero, applyMode, resize, visibilitychange, onPageScroll, filmFallback). Every new branch is behind phoneOn or html.story.pfilm; prove with the pixel diff of desktop stills at three __feel.at() moments, friction-check.js, verify-live.js and the index.html diff (expect only the __PHONE lines, the <picture> and tokens).

Legibility of the thread on the full-bleed props: the 2.2 px body over the white clouds relies on the 5 px black case at .55; check the sky stills at dpr 2 and 3, and if the case reads as a dark line on the cloud raise the glow (.16 -> .22) rather than the case.

The merge trigger fires while the reader is still moving fast (a flick that carries the mark from 80% to 10% of the screen in 300 ms): the loop draws with the 0.5 s floor and the 1.1 s merge runs while the mark is already near the top; acceptable, and the reader who cares scrolls back 10vh and watches it again. Do not try to lock scroll for it.
Hostinger's CDN re-encodes JPEGs (RESUME.md): hero-still-m.jpg and hero-mark-m.jpg will not hash-match live; add them to verify-live.js's visual-compare list and hero-scrub-m.mp4 to the hash list.

Landscape phones (844x390, coarse): the box is 265x331 with a 204 px mark; the first screen's text row is 3 lines short; both are in the probe matrix and are honest small-screen renderings, not defects, but Karan should see the 844x390 sheet before it ships.

What I would NOT do, and why: a 350vh pin (a third flick spent inside the hero is the film holding the page hostage); filter:blur on the live canvas or a 32 px 'soft canvas' (runtime cost or cleverness for a result a 20 KB still gives free); the <video> element as a phone fallback (100-300 ms seeks, stepped scrub, overlay buttons in Samsung Internet); frames 233-239 (the ring opening bottom-right contradicts a thread leaving at the left); a line born from the mark's centre (from nowhere); wide snake waves (the gutter is 20 px and the text edge is sacred); a pure scroll-scrubbed merge (leaves half-merged lockups); an attract loop or any motion at rest under the words; scroll-snap, content-visibility, smooth-scroll changes, an orientation-gated feature, position:fixed for the frame, 100dvh anywhere; touching copy, the desktop or the reduced-motion story.
